newsitem.title: USA: Bright burst may warn Earth of solar storms - report.
newsitem.headline: Bright burst may warn Earth of solar storms - report.

text.p: Solar storms that can disrupt global power and telecommunications may be preceded by a bright burst of solar plasma that could give Earth a 20- to 40-hour warning, a scientist said on Monday.

S. T. Wu, director of the Centre for Space Plasma and Aeronomic Research at the University of Alabama in Huntsville, told an American Geophysical Union conference in San Francisco that scientists at the centre were working to develop ways to predict geomagnetic storms. "We are trying to develop numeric models for predicting these events, just like the models that meteorologists use to predict the weather," he said.

Solar storms can inject highly ionised particles into Earth's magnetic field. These solar bursts can cripple power systems on Earth and have been linked to disruptions to satellites and other telecommunications equipment.

Wu said it appeared that most geomagnetic storms were caused by so-called coronal mass ejections, which occur in the solar atmosphere and result in a bright burst of light. Special instruments aboard satellites could give scientists early warning of a coming storm.
"It takes from 20 hours to two days from when we see the bright outburst until these materials reach the Earth, so we would have time to warn everyone," Wu said.
